### 1. Scene
A mixed meat plate: a cooked bone-in shank, several small pieces of cooked meat, and two portions of breaded fried chicken. Exact meat types are uncertain.

### 2. Vessel
A shallow dinner plate, approximately **26 cm diameter**.  
Area = 3.14 × 13² ≈ **531 cm²**.

### 3–7. Items, area, volume, weight and energy
No separate sauce or pooled oil is visible. Cooking fat and breading are included in the food energy estimates.

| Visible item | Plate area | Area × average height = volume | Density | Estimated weight | kcal/100 g | kcal |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Bone-in cooked shank | 17% | 90 × 2.0 = 180 ml | 0.95 | 171 g including bone | See below | 301 |
| Brown meat slice, upper left | 5% | 27 × 1.0 = 27 ml | 1.0 | 27 g | 230 | 62 |
| Cooked meat piece, left | 6% | 32 × 1.1 = 35 ml | 1.0 | 35 g | 250 | 88 |
| Cooked meat piece, right | 4% | 21 × 1.0 = 21 ml | 1.0 | 21 g | 250 | 53 |
| Breaded chicken, upper right | 7% | 37 × 1.6 = 59 ml | 0.9 | 53 g | 290 | 154 |
| Breaded chicken strip, bottom | 6% | 32 × 1.1 = 35 ml | 0.9 | 32 g | 290 | 93 |

**Area check:** 17 + 5 + 6 + 4 + 7 + 6 = **45% covered**, consistent with the substantial exposed plate.

The shank estimate includes approximately **40 g of inedible bone**, leaving **131 g of edible meat**, estimated at **230 kcal/100 g**. This is a bone allowance, not an additional air-gap reduction.

### 8. Sanity check
Estimated total: **339 g including bone**, or **299 g edible food**, and approximately **750 kcal**. This is plausible for a partly covered plate of mostly meat and fried chicken. A reasonable uncertainty range is roughly **600–900 kcal**.
